detail.longDescription: According to the docs , typing.Final is: Special typing construct to indicate final names to type checkers. Final names cannot be reassigned in any scope. Final names declared in class scopes cannot be overridden in subclasses. And according to this Q&A , constants are written in uppercase by convention and can be annotated with the Final qualifier. My project has a constants.py config file containing uppercase constants. Example: WIDTH = 100 HEIGHT = 150 SPEED = 35 PIN = 4 Should they be annotated with Final ? WIDTH: Final = 100 HEIGHT: Final = 150 SPEED: Final = 35 PIN: Final = 4 Does using Final provide any benefit over the uppercase convention?
